analysis: What changed vs the 4 AM brief: very little is genuinely new — the tape is quiet on the holiday. Futures are a touch softer than the 4 AM IBD readings (Dow +0.2% vs +0.4%, S&P +0.4% vs +0.55%) but still green, Europe's Stoxx 600 jumped 1.7% and gold pushed above $3,570, up more than 1%, with Bitcoin back over $60,000. No fresh company-specific news on the covered names in the last 45 minutes; the story remains Wednesday's historic reversal — the Nasdaq's sharpest intraday comeback since April 2025 and the Dow's largest since February 2022 — plus the rates backdrop (10Y below 4.85% after a 5.4bp drop, December Fed hike priced at 97.9%) and the BoK hike and oil jump carried from overnight. Carried macro: Wednesday's jobless claims fell to 189,000, below the 200,000 forecast and matching this year's low, with continuing claims down 95,000 to 1.697 million — a firm labor read that sits oddly next to a near-certain December hike, and it helps explain why yields fell into the break despite hot inflation. Signal vs noise: the global follow-through, gold's rebound and the claims print are signal; any single futures tick on a closed holiday morning is noise, and Friday's thin half session can amplify the first move either way. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines this morning, so community_signals is empty.

headlines.headline: US index futures hold gains early Thursday on the Thanksgiving holiday: Nasdaq-100 +0.5%, S&P 500 +0.4%, Dow +0.2%, extending Wednesday's late-session rebound.
headlines.why_it_matters: Futures are carrying the dip-buying momentum into the holiday pause — a steadier setup for Friday's thin half session, though overnight futures do not guarantee Friday's open.

headlines.headline: Global rebound broadens: Europe-wide Stoxx 600 jumps 1.7%, and Asian benchmarks closed higher (Nikkei +1.5%, Kospi +1.8%, Taiwan Taiex +2.9%, Hang Seng +2.0%), led by the chip and AI-linked names that sold off hardest Wednesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dip-buying is now global rather than a one-session US bounce — a steadier backdrop for Friday's reopen, with the rebound still modest next to Wednesday's slide (Kospi fell 6.2% Wednesday).

headlines.headline: Gold rallies more than 1% to trade around $3,570 a troy ounce after falling alongside AI stocks in recent weeks; Bitcoin recovers back above $60,000.
headlines.why_it_matters: Metals and crypto stabilizing alongside equities suggests the risk-off pressure is easing across assets, not just in stocks.

headlines.headline: Oil holds near Wednesday's highs: Brent edges 0.4% lower to around $94.30 a barrel, WTI nudges up 0.1% to $83.75, as Houthi-Saudi hostilities keep Red Sea shipping risk in focus.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-risk premium in crude stays in place, adding to the inflation backdrop the Fed is watching into the Dec 8-9 meeting, where a hike is now priced near-certain.

headlines.headline: Treasury yields fell across the curve into the break: the 10-year dropped 5.4bp to trade below 4.85%, and the 2-year/10-year spread sits near its flattest since March 2025; markets price a December Fed hike at 97.9% (LSEG).
headlines.why_it_matters: Yields falling despite hot inflation data and a near-certain December hike says the bond market is pricing growth risk, not just inflation — the tension at the heart of the current tape.
